structural.title: Booking date shows one day earlier on some surfaces and for some recipients
structural.summary: A booked date is shown one calendar day earlier (weekday moving with it, month unchanged) on one surface or to one recipient but not another, consistent with a date-only booking being treated as a timestamp and rendered across a timezone or date boundary.
structural.reason: Every concrete non-swap body shifts in the same direction: R-41202 (calendar Monday 11 May vs invite Tuesday 12 May), R-41620 (Tuesday 6 October shown as Monday) and R-41344 (Toronto viewer gets Monday, Lisbon viewer Tuesday) all show the earlier day, and the earlier day appears on the surface or in the city further west or closer to UTC. That is the signature of one mechanism, a local date serialised as midnight and rendered in another zone, not three. R-41344 is the same bug observed by two viewers at once rather than a distinct per-city defect. R-41209 ('one day off', no direction) fits the same family. R-41236 (invite arrived before the booking was made) names no date, but an invite stamped one day early is exactly what this mechanism produces, the desk filed it as a one-day move, and nothing else in the 412 reports suggests a genuine send-before-commit ordering bug; it is the weakest member and should be marked provisional. Fallback if the lead wants only body-proven members: merge P-shift and P-tz-split, keep R-41236 alone.
structural.confidence: high that P-shift and P-tz-split are one defect (three concrete bodies, same direction, same month); medium that R-41236 belongs with them (mechanism fits, body does not say).
